gartner-hype-cycle-1999-010.note: Jini (1998) never reached 5% of device/organisation use; Sun handed it to Apache River in 2007 (Wikipedia, per builders; WebFetch to wikipedia.org blocked in audit env). Miss at P=2004 holds under any abandonment year.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-011.note: KPMG KM Research Report 2000 (423 large firms, fielded 1999): 38% had a KM programme in place, above 20% before P=2004 (PDF not reachable from audit env; figures consistent across builders). Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-012.note: XML 1.0 W3C Rec 1998, built into DBs/app servers by early 2000s; Yankee Group 2004: 48% of enterprises had deployed XML web services, consistent with 20% routine XML use by 2003 (P+2). Hit, years are estimates.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-014.note: DigiCash: ~5,000 users, bankrupt 1998, assets sold 2002; CyberCash bankrupt 2001 (Wikipedia DigiCash/Ecash). Never near 5%; miss at P=2009.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-015.note: VRML/plug-in 3D web never widely adopted, faded by ~2001-2002 (Wikipedia VRML/Web3D); WebGL is a later generation. Miss at P=2004.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-016.note: Google/Northstar 2014: 41% of adult (smartphone) respondents used voice search daily, about 25% of all US adults given ~60% smartphone ownership; Pew 2017: 46% of US adults use voice assistants. Mainstream 2014 = P+5 with 5% only from ~2010: partial.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-017.note: Chip payment cards universal in France by 1992 (one G7 market mainstream before 1999); UK 2006, US 70% by 2016 (Wikipedia EMV). Hit at P=2004 holds.

gartner-hype-cycle-1999-018.note: Builders used US only (Pew 2004), but Statistics Canada (The Daily, 23 Sep 2003) reports 23.7% of all Canadian households had high-speed internet in 2001, and OECD shows Korea above 11 subs/100 people by March 2001; a G7 market was mainstream at P=2001, the same one-major-market test both builders used for Smart Cards.

gartner-hype-cycle-2000-004.note: Tablet PC pen-first devices failed; pens remain optional accessories (Apple Pencil 2015). No evidence of 5% of units by P=2010 or 50% by 2015. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2001-001.note: Only consumer product was Toshiba Dynario, 3,000 units Japan-only 2009 (Toshiba PR, phys.org per builders). Never 5%; miss at P=2011.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-017.note: Hit needs 20% of large organisations running a BPMS in production by 2012; both builders say no survey gives an adoption share (BPTrends gives interest only), and an audit search found only Forrester tool-mix shares and Gartner process-model use (6% of knowledge workers 2009). Year 2010 is unevidenced.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-018.note: Windows Vista (30 Jan 2007) shipped integrated Windows Search, Spotlight in Mac OS X 2005 (Wikipedia Windows Search); Windows/Mac preinstalls put it on most new PCs by 2007-2008, within P+2=2009. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-019.note: Desktop Linux 4% worldwide Feb 2024, US 5% June 2025 (Wikipedia Linux adoption; StatCounter); below 5% through P+5=2015, never 20%. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-020.note: Toshiba Dynario 3,000-unit Japan test (2009) was the only consumer launch; vendors missed launch targets (Electronic Design). Never 5%; miss at P=2015.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-025.note: All WiMAX variants peaked ~20M subscribers worldwide (2011), a small fraction of broadband; Yota to LTE 2010, Sprint dropped WiMAX 2012 (Wikipedia WiMAX). Miss at P=2010.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-026.note: Pew: 36% of US internet users used Wikipedia in Feb 2007, 53% in 2010 (Pew 2011 / phys.org); mainstream before P=2010 under the consumer reading, and enterprise wikis by ~2008-2010 under the other. Hit either way.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-027.note: Omdia: AMOLED passed 50% of smartphone displays only in 2024 (P+14); iSuppli via oled-info: 47.4M AMOLED units shipped in 2010 against ~300M smartphones, so at least 5% by P=2010. Partial.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-030.note: TPM 2.0 required on all new Windows device models from 28 July 2016 (Wikipedia TPM); >100M TPM PCs in 2007 (Dark Reading). Mainstream by 2016 at latest, within P+2=2017. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-031.note: Avasant 2006: 19% of organisations had implemented SOA; Gartner 2008 (GovTech): near-universal among large European firms. 20% by ~2007, before P=2010. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-033.note: Tablet PCs (2003) stayed a $2,000+ niche, superseded by iPad 2010 (Wikipedia Microsoft Tablet PC); no evidence of 5% of notebook shipments. Miss at P=2010 regardless of abandonment flag.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-034.note: SEC phased XBRL in 2009-2011 to all US public filers; FDIC bank call reports from 2005; UK iXBRL 2011 (Wikipedia XBRL). Mainstream by 2011, within P+2=2012. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-035.note: Accenture 2018: 28% of North American retailers at full RFID adoption (46% piloting), 47% in 2020; 5% passed well before P=2015. No evidence of full adoption at 20% by 2017, so partial (5% by P; mainstream ~P+3) is the supported verdict under the dominant supply-chain reading.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-036.note: Pew (Oct 2010): 20% of US internet users had made online video calls by April 2009, 23% in 2010. Mainstream before P=2010. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-039.note: Pew 2013: 74% of US smartphone owners use location services; smartphone ownership 35% in 2011 (Pew fact sheet) gives ~20-26% of adults by 2011-2012, within P+2=2012. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-040.note: Hit needs 20% of banks/insurers running a rules engine in production by 2009; both builders cite only Wikipedia saying engines date from the early 1990s and are typical in finance/insurance, and an audit search found no adoption survey. Mainstream year 2007/2008 is unevidenced.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-041.note: FCC Local Telephone Competition (Dec 2008, DOC-299052A1) gives 19.2M residential interconnected VoIP subscriptions, about a fifth of residential voice lines by 2008-2009, within P+2=2009; enterprise IP-PBX shipments passed half earlier. Primary pages not fetchable (egress blocked); verified via search summaries. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-042.note: Builders picked a handset test, but TTS shipped built into Windows XP (Narrator/SAPI 5, Microsoft Sam) and every Mac OS X release, i.e. on well over 50% of new PCs before 2007 (Wikipedia: Microsoft text-to-speech voices, PlainTalk; builder A's own note says so). Under D16's device-feature test it was already mainstream at placed year 2007, so hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-043.note: Call Centre Helper/ContactBabel (2012): 10% of contact centres used speech recognition in IVR (23% of large ones), never 20% by 2012 = P+5; speech IVR at large telcos/airlines/banks from about 2000 makes at least 5% by 2007 plausible though not measured directly. Partial.

gartner-hype-cycle-2005-044.note: A 2005 survey of 403 US IT professionals found 64% of their organisations used web services to integrate internal applications (cited in 'Web Services: the third wave of internet development', ResearchGate), above 20% by 2005. The builders' META Group cite was a forecast, but the hit holds.

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-012.note: Wii (Nov 2006, 101M+ units, accelerometer/IR gesture input) and Kinect (2010) were the dominant 2007 meaning; US Wii installed base passed a fifth of households around 2009, well before P+2=2019. Wikipedia pages not fetchable here (egress blocked); facts are well documented. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-013.note: Both builders grade a 'distinct tool category' reading and both state that the other faithful 2007 reading (web apps combining third-party APIs, per Wikipedia 'Mashup (web application hybrid)') became routine web practice by about 2010, which would be a hit; no measurement supports either, so the miss rests on an unmeasured reading choice (D16 unfalsifiable test not resolved).

gartner-hype-cycle-2007-014.note: Second Life peaked at about 1M regular users (Wikipedia; Time 2021: about 750k MAU), and Pew 2008 found 2% of adult gamers had visited a virtual world; far below 5% of internet users by P+5=2022 under the dominant 2007 (Second Life-style) reading. Game platforms (Roblox) are a different reading. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-020.note: The partial depends entirely on an estimated year_5pct of 2010; neither builder nor my search found any survey of idea-management platform adoption (only vendor market reports and a Gartner 'nearing mainstream' blog), so neither at least 5% by 2013 nor below 5% is supported.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-022.note: Pew 'Wikipedia, past and present' (2011): 36% of US online adults used Wikipedia in Feb 2007 and 53% in May 2010, above 20% before P=2013; enterprise wiki reading also mainstream by then. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-023.note: Pew 'E-Reading Rises as Device Ownership Jumps' (Jan 2014): e-reader (Kindle/Nook) ownership 24% of US adults in Sept 2013 and 32% in Jan 2014, so the e-paper device proxy passed 20% by P=2013 (some LCD Nook/Kindle models inflate it slightly). Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-024.note: Microsoft-spec pen Tablet PCs stayed a costly niche (Dell Latitude XT at $2,500 in 2007, Nextgov 2006; Gartner's 2002 forecast of 37% of notebooks by 2007 never came close); later Windows 2-in-1s came after P=2013 and never reached 50% of notebooks by 2018. Miss under the dominant 2008 reading (not iPad-style tablets).

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-025.note: Avasant 'SOA Adoption Trends' (2006) exists and describes early-stage adoption (builder B cites 19% implemented); with Forrester's 44% by 2008 cited by builder A, SOA in production passed 20% by about 2007, before P=2013. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-026.note: Pew 'Location-Based Services' (Sept 2013): 74% of US adult smartphone owners use location-based directions/information; with smartphone ownership at 35% (2011) and 56% (2013) per Pew, that is about 26-41% of adults by 2011-2013, within P+2. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2008-027.note: A 2005 survey of 403 US IT professionals found 64% of organisations used web services for internal application integration (cited in 'Web Services: the third wave', ResearchGate), so SOAP/XML web services were mainstream before P=2010. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-002.note: DisplaySearch via Wikipedia '3D television': 24.1M 3D TVs in 2011 and 41.5M in 2012 against about 240M TVs (10-17%), never 50% of new units; production ended 2016 and Sony/LG dropped 3D in Jan 2017, before P=2019. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-004.note: CoDA is a Gartner-defined architectural style (Gartner IT glossary) with no product category or adoption measure; Gartner replaced it with 'context-enriched services' in 2011. Nothing shows 5% of organisations on a formal CoDA by 2024 = P+5. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2009-005.note: comScore via TechCrunch (Dec 2008): YouTube handled 2.73bn US searches in Nov 2008, 25.4% of Google-site searches; Pew (2010): 69% of US internet users watched online video by 2009. Video search was mass behaviour long before P=2019. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2010-030.note: Second Life-style public social worlds stayed at about 0.5-1M users (Wikipedia; Time 2021), far below 5% of internet users through P+5=2025. Roblox/Fortnite-style game worlds would count only under a broader gaming reading that was not dominant for 'public virtual worlds' in 2010. Miss.

gartner-hype-cycle-2013-004.note: Pew short read (Jan 2020; survey 3-17 June 2019, n=4,272): 21% of US adults regularly wear a smartwatch or fitness tracker, mainstream in 2019, within P+2=2020. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-040.note: RTInsights survey ('Why the Move to In-Memory Technology?', mid-2010s): about 28% of organisations employed in-memory technologies and 23% more were piloting; together with default in-memory engines in Power BI, Qlik and Tableau, this supports at least 20% by P+2=2018. Builders cited no survey; the verdict holds. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-041.note: Microsoft Teams (activity feed built in) was used by 500,000 organisations including 91 of the Fortune 100 by March 2019 (VentureBeat/TechCrunch), and a 2019 Spiceworks survey expected 41% of organisations on Teams by 2020; at least 20% routine use is reached by P+2=2021 at the latest. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-042.note: PwC/Manufacturing Institute 'The new shape of industrial manufacturing' (June 2014, NIST-hosted PDF): 25% of US manufacturers used 3D printing for prototyping only, 10% for prototyping and production, 1% for final parts only (about 35% routine use) in 2014, before P=2019. Eurostat's 4% of all EU enterprises uses a broader population. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2014-045.note: Google/Northstar Mobile Voice Study (Oct 2014, PR Newswire): 41% of US adult smartphone users used voice search daily; Pew (Dec 2017): 46% of US adults used voice assistants. Mainstream by 2014-2017, within P+2=2018. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2016-026.note: McKinsey Global AI Survey (Nov 2019): 47% (2018) and 58% (2019) of respondents' organisations embedded at least one AI capability; O'Reilly 'AI adoption in the enterprise 2020': 27% mature in 2019, over half in 2020. Well above 20% by P=2021 despite sample skew. Hit.

gartner-hype-cycle-2016-031.note: Pew short read (Dec 2017): 46% of US adults used digital voice assistants, which mainly answer spoken questions; LLM chat assistants added mass use from 2023. Mainstream by 2017, before P=2021. Hit.

note: Cloud session 2026-10-01: the network policy blocked direct page fetches, so the auditors checked cited sources through search-result summaries, not the pages. Two auditor agents, 25 claims each.
